beats.title: Chariots Clash at Kadesh
beats.description: Thousands of horse-drawn war chariots met in the largest chariot battle ever recorded, between Egypt and the Hittites.
beats.note: Some sources give 1275 BCE; most give about 1274.

beats.title: Syracuse Builds the First Catapults
beats.description: The tyrant of a Sicilian city gathered engineers to invent machines that hurled bolts and stones at enemy walls.
beats.note: Traditional date; whether Dionysius truly invented it is debated.

beats.title: Sarissa Phalanx Wins at Chaeronea
beats.description: Phalanxes bristling with very long pikes helped a Macedonian king crush the united Greek city-states.

beats.title: Hannibal's Elephants Cross the Alps
beats.description: A Carthaginian general led war elephants over the mountains to strike at Rome from the north.

beats.title: Archimedes Defends Syracuse
beats.description: A Greek inventor was said to have used cranes, giant catapults and burning mirrors against a besieging Roman fleet.
beats.note: Siege began 213 BCE by the usual dating; some give 214.

beats.title: Greek Fire Used at Constantinople
beats.description: Byzantine ships sprayed a secret burning liquid that clung to water and set enemy fleets ablaze.
beats.note: Siege ran 674-678; some place first use at Cyzicus in 673. Uses the siege start, as in the theme example.

beats.title: Gunpowder Recipe Written Down
beats.description: A Chinese military manual set out formulas for mixing saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal into a weapon powder.
beats.note: Earliest known written gunpowder formula in a military text.

beats.title: Exploding Bombs Meet the Samurai
beats.description: Mongol invaders hurled iron shells filled with gunpowder at astonished Japanese warriors on the shore.

beats.title: Longbows and Cannon Win at Crecy
beats.description: English archers with huge bows, plus a few early cannon, cut down charging French knights.

beats.title: Hussite War Wagons Hold the Line
beats.description: Rebels in Bohemia chained armoured farm carts into mobile forts and beat repeated cavalry charges.
beats.note: First recorded use at Sudomer, March 1420.

beats.title: The Great Bombard Breaks the Walls
beats.description: A monstrous Ottoman cannon pounded the ancient defences of a great Christian capital until they fell.

beats.title: Leonardo Sketches an Armoured Car
beats.description: An Italian polymath drew a domed, cannon-bristling car driven by crank, a forerunner of the tank.
beats.note: Most sources say 1487; some say about 1485.

beats.title: Matchlock Volleys at Nagashino
beats.description: Massed Japanese gunners fired in rotation from behind fences and shattered a famed samurai cavalry.

beats.title: Light Field Guns Win at Breitenfeld
beats.description: A Swedish king's mobile, quick-firing cannon outgunned heavier imperial artillery in a decisive Protestant victory.

beats.title: Puckle Gun Patented
beats.description: A London lawyer patented a tripod-mounted revolving flintlock, with round bullets for Christians and square for Turks.

beats.title: Shrapnel Shell Invented
beats.description: A British officer devised an artillery shell packed with musket balls that burst above enemy troops.

beats.title: Colt Patents the Revolver
beats.description: A young American gunmaker won a patent for a pistol whose rotating cylinder fired many shots without reloading.

beats.title: Minie Ball Rifle Bullet Designed
beats.description: A French army captain designed a cone-shaped bullet that made rifles quick to load and deadly at long range.

beats.title: Armstrong Breech-Loading Gun
beats.description: An English engineer produced a rifled artillery piece loaded from the rear, far more accurate than old cannon.

beats.title: Gatling Gun Patented
beats.description: A hand-cranked weapon with rotating barrels poured out a stream of bullets, a step toward the machine gun.

beats.title: Maxim Machine Gun Unveiled
beats.description: An American inventor in London made a gun that used its own recoil to load and fire continuously.

beats.title: First Bomb Dropped from a Plane
beats.description: An Italian pilot tossed small grenades by hand onto enemy troops in North Africa, opening the air-war era.

beats.title: Poison Gas Rolls Over Ypres
beats.description: Clouds of chlorine drifted toward Allied trenches, introducing chemical weapons to the battlefield.

beats.title: Tanks Debut at the Somme
beats.description: Lumbering armoured vehicles crawled across no man's land for the first time, to terrify defenders.

beats.title: Thompson Submachine Gun Introduced
beats.description: The 'Tommy gun' with its drum magazine arrived, later famed in the hands of gangsters and soldiers.

beats.title: Spitfire Takes Its First Flight
beats.description: A graceful elliptical-winged British fighter made its maiden flight and became a symbol of resistance.

beats.title: Bouncing Bombs Breach the Dams
beats.description: Bombers skimmed low over reservoirs and released spinning bombs that skipped across water to burst German dams.

beats.title: Me 262 Jet Fighter Enters Combat
beats.description: A swept-wing German aircraft with no propeller outpaced every Allied fighter in the sky.

beats.title: AK-47 Designed
beats.description: A Soviet tank sergeant's simple, rugged assault rifle was finished and went on to become the most produced firearm.

beats.title: B-52 Stratofortress Enters Service
beats.description: An eight-engined American bomber began a career that has outlasted nearly every other aircraft of its age.
beats.note: First operational B-52B delivered 1955; prototype flew 1952.

beats.title: M16 Rifle Adopted
beats.description: A light, black plastic-stocked American rifle replaced wooden-stocked designs and went to jungle war.
beats.note: Air Force adopted 1964; Army formal designation 1965.

beats.title: M1 Abrams Tank Enters Service
beats.description: A turbine-powered American main battle tank with composite armour joined the front-line forces.

beats.title: F-117 Stealth Fighter in Service
beats.description: A faceted black American jet designed to be nearly invisible to radar became operational in secret.

beats.title: B-2 Stealth Bomber Flies
beats.description: A huge flying-wing bomber, built to slip past air defences unseen, took to the air for the first time.

beats.title: Patriot Missiles Face Scuds
beats.description: Television audiences watched anti-missile interceptors rise to meet incoming ballistic missiles over the Gulf.

beats.title: Predator Fires Its First Hellfire
beats.description: An unmanned American aircraft fired a Hellfire missile for the first time, turning a spy drone into a hunter-killer.
beats.note: First Hellfire firing was a February 2001 test; combat strikes followed from late 2001 and 2002, sources disagree on the first.

beats.title: Stuxnet Cyberweapon Discovered
beats.description: A computer worm found to have sabotaged centrifuges showed that software could damage physical machinery.

beats.title: Iron Dome Stops Its First Rocket
beats.description: A mobile Israeli system fired interceptors that destroyed short-range rockets in mid-air over cities.

beats.title: Mother of All Bombs Used in Combat
beats.description: The largest non-nuclear bomb in the American arsenal was dropped in anger for the first time.
beats.note: 13 April 2017. Non-nuclear, so not Atomic Age.

beats.title: Drones Decide Nagorno-Karabakh
beats.description: Cheap Turkish and Israeli attack drones destroyed tanks and air defences in a South Caucasus war.
beats.note: War began 27 September 2020; whether drones were decisive is debated.
